TULSA, Okla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Helmerich & Payne, Inc. (NYSE:HP):

Operating and Financial Highlights for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026

  • H&P announced consolidated revenue of $1.1 billion, reflecting 6% sequential growth.
  • Consolidated net loss attributable to Helmerich & Payne, Inc. of $490 million, or $4.91 loss per share, which includes a $610 million non-cash asset impairment charge for assets primarily located in the Middle East. Adjusted for select items, adjusted net income(1) was $36 million, or $0.36 per share.
  • Consolidated adjusted EBITDA(2) totaled $269 million, increasing 14% sequentially.
  • North America Solutions (NAS) reported operating income of $151 million and achieved direct margin(3) of $259 million, increasing 7% sequentially.
  • Announced the expanded deployment of FlexRobotics® to nine rigs working for ExxonMobil in the Lower 48, phased through 2027.
  • International Solutions reported an operating loss of approximately $648 million and achieved direct margin(3) of $42 million, increasing 34% sequentially.
  • Offshore Solutions reported operating income of approximately $17 million and achieved direct margin(3) of $34 million, increasing 18% sequentially.
  • Approximately $25 million returned to shareholders as part of the Company’s ongoing dividend program.

Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights

  • Fiscal year consolidated revenue of $4.1 billion.
  • Fiscal year net loss attributable to Helmerich & Payne, Inc. of $569 million.
  • Fiscal year adjusted EBITDA(2) of $913 million.
  • Completed the sale of Utica Square, generating approximately $100 million in after-tax proceeds and retired $400 million term loan facility ahead of schedule.
  • Gross capital expenditures of $287 million, within the $270 - $310 million guidance range.

Management Commentary

“I am proud of H&P’s fiscal 2026 performance and the strong finish we delivered,” said President and CEO Trey Adams. “In the fourth quarter, direct margins were at or above the high end of our guidance ranges across all segments.

“As we enter fiscal 2027, we maintain a constructive outlook. Our diversified operations and differentiated technology offerings continue to position us well despite ongoing market volatility. We expect numerous growth opportunities across key markets to drive stronger overall direct margins compared to fiscal 2026.

“In North America Solutions, activity continued to increase with an average of 151 rigs operating during the quarter, while daily margins also improved,” Adams said. “Stronger contract economics reflect the competitive strength of our super-spec fleet and our ability to deliver value to customers. Technology remains another key differentiator. Last month, we announced an expanded collaboration with ExxonMobil to deploy FlexRobotics® on a total of nine rigs. These dynamics, coupled with ongoing super-spec rig market tightness, strengthen our competitive position as we enter fiscal 2027.

“In International Solutions, direct margins improved meaningfully on a sequential basis, as strong growth in Argentina complemented improving margins in our Middle East operations,” said Adams. “Looking ahead, we expect momentum in the Vaca Muerta to continue as we mobilize three rigs from the U.S., lifting our rig count to 15, with several opportunities to expand further.

"We expect Middle East activity to remain subdued through 2027. Following recent notifications of conventional rig suspensions in Saudi Arabia, we now expect to operate an average of 19 rigs through the first fiscal quarter, with the potential for further activity reductions over the course of the year. We will continue to right-size our operational footprint and improve our cost structure as we focus on delivering differentiated results drilling unconventional and complex wells globally. Despite these reductions, we remain committed to driving strong year-over-year growth in direct margins.

“Our Offshore Solutions segment continued to deliver strong results, supported by consistent execution and the achievement of several performance-related bonuses. The long-term contract portfolio provides earnings visibility into fiscal 2027 and beyond."

Senior Vice President and CFO Todd Scruggs added, “2026 demonstrated our ability to remain fiscally disciplined and advance our financial priorities in a dynamic operating environment. During the year, we retired our acquisition-related term loan ahead of schedule, completed the sale of Utica Square, and initiated several Enterprise Optimization programs, and ended the year with $250 million of cash and cash equivalents.

“As we enter fiscal 2027, our capital allocation priorities remain focused on strengthening the balance sheet, maintaining our base dividend, and investing selectively in opportunities that support long-term growth,” Scruggs said. “The combination of strong margin growth and low capital spending levels will enable us to achieve our target of approximately 1x net debt to adjusted EBITDA by calendar year-end 2027.”

“Our leading fleet, differentiated technology solutions, and diversified global operations position us well for the year ahead,” Adams concluded. “We remain focused on disciplined execution and delivering long-term value for shareholders.”

Operating Segment Results for the Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026

North America Solutions: Realized operating income of $151 million, compared with $140 million in the previous quarter. Direct margin(3) increased to $259 million, versus $241 million the previous quarter. On a per-day basis, direct margins averaged $18,657 with 151 rigs active for the fourth fiscal quarter. Results were negatively impacted by a non-recurring inventory write-down charge of approximately $4 million.

International Solutions: Recorded operating loss of approximately $648 million, which included a $606 million asset impairment, compared with a loss of approximately $54 million in the prior quarter. Direct margin(3) improved to $42 million, up from $31 million last quarter. Results included the impact of a non-recurring inventory write-down charge and an accrual related to certain outstanding claims of approximately $2 million. During the fourth quarter we had an average of 66 rigs working.

Offshore Solutions: Reported operating income of approximately $17 million, in line with the previous quarter. Direct margin(3) was $34 million, up from $29 million last quarter, driven by strong performance-related bonuses. We had three active rigs and 29 management contracts in operation during the quarter.

Select Items(4) Included in Net Income per Diluted Share

Fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 net loss of $4.91 per diluted share included a net impact of $5.27 loss per share in after-tax gains and losses comprised of the following:

  • $0.01 of non-cash after-tax gain related to investment securities
  • $0.01 of non-cash after-tax gain related to the change in actuarial assumptions on estimated liabilities
  • $0.00 of after-tax loss related to restructuring charges
  • $(0.02) of after-tax loss related to acquisition transaction and integration costs
  • $(0.07) of after-tax loss related to voluntary separation program charges
  • $(5.20) of non-cash after-tax loss related to asset impairment charges

Third quarter of fiscal year 2026 net income of $0.74 per diluted share included a net impact of $0.85 per share in after-tax gains and losses comprised of the following:

  • $0.88 of after-tax gain related to a real estate asset sale
  • $0.10 of after-tax gain related to involuntary conversion
  • $0.03 of non-cash after-tax gain related to the change in actuarial assumptions on estimated liabilities
  • $(0.01) of non-cash after-tax loss related to asset impairment charges
  • $(0.01) of after-tax loss related to restructuring charges
  • $(0.01) of after-tax loss related to acquisition transaction and integration costs
  • $(0.13) of non-cash after-tax loss related to investment securities

Saudi Arabia Long Lived Asset Impairment

During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Company identified indicators of impairment related to its Saudi Arabia T-Series asset group, including associated equipment, parts and supplies and customer relationship intangible assets. These developments resulted in a one-time non-cash impairment charge of $529.4 million, consisting of $456.8 million related to property, plant and equipment, $58.0 million related to customer relationship intangible assets and $14.6 million related to inventory.

The impairment charge relates to the 30-rig Saudi T-Series asset group and excludes the Company's Saudi FlexRigs, Oman operations, and six T-Series rigs classified as held-for-sale. While the impairment charge did not require a current-period cash outlay, the revised outlook reflects lower expected future cash flows from these operations, which continue to incur maintenance expenditures and costs associated with suspended rigs.

About Helmerich & Payne, Inc.

Founded in 1920, Helmerich & Payne, Inc. (H&P) (NYSE: HP) is committed to delivering industry leading levels of drilling productivity and reliability. H&P operates with the highest level of integrity, safety and innovation to deliver superior results for its customers and returns for shareholders. Through its subsidiaries, the Company designs, fabricates and operates high-performance drilling rigs in conventional and unconventional plays around the world. H&P also develops and implements advanced automation, directional drilling and survey management technologies. As of November 18, 2026, H&P's fleet includes 202 land rigs in the United States, 95 international land rigs and four offshore platform rigs, plus operating 29 offshore management contracts. For more information, see H&P online at www.hpinc.com.

Key Terms

adjusted ebitdafinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.
asset impairment chargefinancial
An asset impairment charge is an accounting entry that reduces the reported value of a company’s asset when its expected future benefits have fallen significantly — like marking down spoiled inventory or a damaged piece of equipment. For investors, it matters because the charge cuts reported profits and lowers the company’s net asset value, signaling that some expected cash flows or benefits from that asset are no longer likely to materialize.
term loanfinancial
A term loan is a type of loan that is borrowed for a set period of time, with a fixed schedule for repaying the money, usually in regular payments. It matters to investors because it represents a company's borrowing costs and financial stability; reliable repayment of these loans can indicate strong financial health, while difficulties may signal potential risks.
capital expendituresfinancial
Capital expenditures are the money a company spends to buy or improve big assets like buildings, equipment, or machines that will last a long time. These investments matter because they help the company grow and operate more efficiently, similar to how upgrading a home’s appliances or adding a new room can make it better and more valuable.

RACINE, Wis., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Modexus Solutions (NYSE: MOD), a diversified global leader in thermal management technology and solutions, today hosted an Investor Day to provide an in-depth review of the Company's strategy, including growth opportunities across its Data Centers and Commercial HVAC (CHVAC) businesses, and provided multi-year financial targets.

During the event, executive leadership highlighted the strategic pillars driving the Company's compounding growth and long-term shareholder value creation:

  • Differentiated, Highly Engineered Solutions: Capitalizing on more than a century of deep expertise in thermal management to drive innovative, customer-centric solutions.

  • Expanding End Markets: Driving rapid growth by positioning the Company in favorable markets with evolving thermal requirements.

  • 80/20 Culture: Combining a high-performance culture with 80/20 discipline to evolve our portfolio and deliver sustainable, compounding shareholder value.

"Today we presented an exciting new chapter in our transformation as we build on more than 100 years of thermal management expertise to position Modexus Solutions for its next phase of compounding growth," said President and Chief Executive Officer, Neil D. Brinker. "The deliberate actions we have taken to evolve our portfolio have created a focused, high growth business with differentiated capabilities in mission-critical markets. With accelerating demand for advanced cooling solutions for data centers and commercial HVAC applications, we are leveraging our customer partnerships, technology leadership, and 80/20 discipline to drive profitable growth. We believe we are still in the early stages of realizing our full potential and are confident in our ability to create substantial long-term value for our customers and shareholders."

Fiscal 2029 Long-Term Financial Targets
During the presentation, Modexus Solutions established the following multi-year financial targets:

  • Revenue Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR): 40 percent to 55 percent over the three-year period for the total company from the beginning of fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029, excluding any incremental acquisitions. This is supported by an expectation of 60 percent to 80 percent revenue growth in Data Centers and 7 percent to 10 percent revenue growth in Commercial HVAC over the same period.

  • Adjusted EBITDA Margin: 19 percent to 21 percent for the total company in fiscal 2029. This is supported by expected fiscal 2029 adjusted EBITDA margins of 22 percent to 24 percent in Data Centers and 20 percent to 22 percent in Commercial HVAC.

"Our new financial targets reflect the extraordinary commercial momentum across our business and our disciplined execution," stated Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Mick Lucareli. "Targeting a 40% to 55% three-year revenue CAGR for the total company alongside adjusted EBITDA margins of 19% to 21% in fiscal 2029 demonstrates the earnings power of our operating model. This trajectory is supported by unprecedented demand and robust backlog in Data Centers, sustained growth across Commercial HVAC, and systematic margin enhancement across our operating footprint. Backed by disciplined capital deployment and a strong balance sheet, Modexus Solutions is uniquely positioned to deliver significant earnings expansion and compound shareholder value over the long term."

A webcast replay of the Investor Day presentations, along with the accompanying slide deck and event transcript, will be accessible on the Investor Relations section of the Modexus Solutions website at investors.modexussolutions.com/.

Modexus Solutions develops thermal innovations that lead the pace of progress. Since 1916, we have been the go-to partner in thermal management, enabling customers to reach new frontiers through engineering excellence, proprietary technologies, and collaborative systems design. Driven by the dedication of more than 9,000 employees worldwide, our portfolio of advanced commercial HVAC and data center cooling solutions delivers breakthroughs that accelerate societal progress and advance our purpose of Engineering a Cleaner, Healthier World™. The Company defines adjusted EBITDA margin as adjusted EBITDA divided by net sales. The company uses these non-GAAP financial measures and other key metrics internally in analyzing its financial results and believes that the use of these non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics are helpful to investors as an additional tool to evaluate ongoing operating results and trends, and in comparing the company's financial results with other companies in its industry, many of which present similar non-GAAP financial measures or key metrics.

The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics are not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for comparable GAAP financial measures and should be read only in conjunction with the company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of the company's historical non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release, and investors are encouraged to review these reconciliations.

Non-GAAP operating income. Palo Alto Networks defines non-GAAP operating income as operating income plus share-based compensation-related charges, including share-based payroll tax expense, acquisition-related costs, including change in fair value of contingent consideration liability, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, and litigation-related charges. The company believes that non-GAAP operating income provides management and investors with greater visibility into the underlying performance of the company's core business operating results.

Non-GAAP net income and net income per share, diluted. Palo Alto Networks defines non-GAAP net income as net income plus share-based compensation-related charges, including share-based payroll tax expense, acquisition-related costs, including change in fair value of contingent consideration liability, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, litigation-related charges, and change in fair value of convertible senior notes and capped calls. The company also excludes from non-GAAP income tax and other tax adjustments related to our long-term non-GAAP effective tax rate in order to provide a complete picture of the company's recurring core business operating results. The company defines non-GAAP net income per share, diluted, as non-GAAP net income divided by the weighted-average diluted shares outstanding, which includes the potentially dilutive effect of the company's employee equity incentive plan awards and the company's convertible senior notes and related warrants, after giving effect to the anti-dilutive impact of the company's note hedge agreements and capped call transactions, which reduced the potential economic dilution that otherwise would have occurred in connection with the conversion and settlement of the company's convertible senior notes. Under GAAP, the anti-dilutive impact of the note hedge or capped calls is not reflected in diluted shares outstanding. The company considers these non-GAAP financial measures to be useful metrics for management and investors for the same reasons that it uses non-GAAP operating income.

Adjusted free cash flow margin, adjusted free cash flow, and free cash flow. Palo Alto Networks defines adjusted free cash flow margin, a non-GAAP measure, as adjusted free cash flow divided by total revenue. The company defines adjusted free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, as free cash flow, plus certain capital expenditures for our headquarters and certain corporate assets, plus payments of acquisition-related costs, plus litigation-related payments. The company defines free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, as net cash provided by operating activities less purchases of property, equipment, and other assets. We consider free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow margin to be operating metrics as well as liquidity measures that provide useful information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated by the business after necessary capital expenditures and before the impact of certain qualifying non-recurring cash payments from operating activities, as applicable. A limitation of the utility of free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow as a measure of our liquidity is that it does not represent the total increase or decrease in our cash balance for the period. In addition, it is important to note that other companies, including companies in our industry, may not use free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow, may calculate free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow in a different manner than we do, or may use other financial measures to evaluate their liquidity, all of which could reduce the usefulness of free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow as a comparative measure.

Next-Generation Security ARR. Palo Alto Networks defines Next-Generation Security ARR as the annualized allocated revenue of all active contracts as of the final day of the reporting period related to all product, subscription and support offerings, excluding revenue from hardware products, and legacy attached subscriptions, support offerings and professional services. The company considers Next-Generation Security ARR to be a useful operating metric for management and investors to assess the performance of the company because Next-Generation Security is where the company has focused its innovation and the company expects its overall revenue to be disproportionately driven by this Next-Generation Security portfolio. Because Next-Generation Security ARR does not have the effect of providing a numerical measure that is different from any comparable GAAP measure, the company does not consider it a non-GAAP measure.

Investors are cautioned that there are a number of limitations associated with the use of non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics as analytical tools. Many of the adjustments to the company's GAAP financial measures reflect the exclusion of items that are recurring and will be reflected in the company's financial results for the foreseeable future, such as share-based compensation, which is an important part of Palo Alto Networks employees' compensation and impacts their performance. Furthermore, these non-GAAP financial measures are not based on any standardized methodology prescribed by GAAP, and the components that Palo Alto Networks excludes in its calculation of non-GAAP financial measures may differ from the components that its peer companies exclude when they report their non-GAAP results of operations. As a result, these non-GAAP financial measures may not be directly comparable to similar non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies. Palo Alto Networks compensates for these limitations by providing specific information regarding the GAAP amounts excluded from these non-GAAP financial measures. In the future, the company may also exclude non-recurring expenses and other expenses that do not reflect the company's core business operating results.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Everpure (NYSE: P), the company revolutionizing storage and data management, today announced financial results for its third quarter fiscal year 2027 ended November 1, 2026.

"The strength of our Q3 results reinforces Everpure's role as the trusted partner customers rely on for their most critical data infrastructure," said Charles Giancarlo, Chairman and CEO of Everpure. "As organizations work to break down data silos and modernize their data estates, our growth across both core and new, high-growth markets shows we are uniquely equipped to solve their most complex data challenges at scale."

Third Quarter Financial Highlights

  • Revenue $1.5 billion, up 51% year-over-year
  • Product revenue $948 million, up 77% year-over-year
  • Subscription services revenue $512 million, up 19% year-over-year
  • Subscription annual recurring revenue (ARR) $2.2 billion, up 20% year-over-year
  • Remaining performance obligations (RPO) $4.2 billion, up 44% year-over-year
  • GAAP gross margin 68.0%; non-GAAP gross margin 69.2%
  • GAAP operating income $150 million; non-GAAP operating income $345 million
  • GAAP operating margin 10.3%; non-GAAP operating margin 23.6%
  • Operating cash flow $443 million; free cash flow $265 million
  • Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities $1.1 billion
  • Returned approximately $67 million to stockholders through share repurchases of 0.5 million shares.

"Q3 marked another outstanding quarter of execution for Everpure, where we delivered record revenue and operating income, exceeding the high end of our guidance," said Everpure CFO Tarek Robbiati. "Our results reflect the strength of our diversified portfolio, with our core and core AI offerings complemented by increasing contributions from our new businesses. We are raising full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter and reiterating our strong preliminary FY28 outlook, underscoring confidence in our durable business model and broad-based momentum."

Third Quarter Company Highlights

Advancing Data Primacy

  • Expanded Everpure Data Intelligence with native Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration and privacy-first file intelligence, giving AI agents secure, governed access to live enterprise data context.
  • Released the Global Data Sovereignty Report 2026, finding that while 90% of surveyed enterprises recognize data sovereignty as a business concern, 64% lack a formal data sovereignty strategy.

Driving Hyperscaler Adoption and Industry-Leading AI Performance

  • Secured a design win with a second top-five hyperscaler, validating Everpure DirectFlash® technology in the world's largest cloud environments.
  • FlashBlade//EXA ranked first on every checkpointing and KV-cache metric submitted in the MLPerf Storage v3.0 closed division.
  • Introduced PureKVA on FlashBlade, delivering faster time to first token for large language model inference.

Industry and Market Recognition

  • Joined the S&P 500 index in September 2026.
  • Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Storage Platforms, positioned highest in execution and furthest in vision for the second consecutive year.
  • Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Infrastructure Platform Consumption Services, positioned highest in execution and furthest in vision for the second consecutive year.
  • Named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Container Data and Infrastructure Management Software (November 2026).
  • Named one of Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology 2026.

TEMPE, Ariz. & SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Align Technology, Inc. (“Align”) (Nasdaq: ALGN), a leading global medical device company that designs, manufactures, and sells the Invisalign® System of clear aligners, iTero™ intraoral scanners, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software for digital orthodontics and restorative dentistry, today announced that its Board of Directors has appointed Paul J. Clancy, a biopharmaceutical executive and former Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Biogen Inc., as a director effective immediately and Ian Bell, Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of Alcon Inc., as a director effective December 10, 2026.

Paul J. Clancy

“We are pleased to welcome Paul Clancy to our Board and look forward to the addition of Ian Bell in December,” said Kevin Conroy, Chairman of the Board of Align Technology. “Paul and Ian bring significant global healthcare, financial, innovation and operational leadership experience that will complement the strengths of Align’s Board. Paul’s deep financial and strategic leadership in the biopharmaceutical industry, together with Ian’s broad perspective across commercial, manufacturing, quality and regulatory operations and his experience leading innovation-driven businesses, will be valuable as we continue to execute our strategy and drive long-term growth.”

Mr. Clancy brings more than 30 years of strategic, financial and operational leadership experience, primarily in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries. He served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Alexion Pharmaceuticals from July 2017 to October 2019 and remained a Senior Advisor to the company until July 2020. Previously, he served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Biogen from 2007 to 2017, where he led the company's financial strategy through a decade of growth. After joining Biogen in 2001 as Vice President of U.S. Marketing, he held several other senior leadership roles, including Vice President of Portfolio Management and Senior Vice President of Finance, with responsibility for treasury, tax, investor relations and business planning. Before Biogen, Mr. Clancy spent 13 years at PepsiCo in a range of finance, strategy and general management positions. He currently serves on the board of directors of Incyte Corporation, where he chairs the Audit and Finance Committee, and as Chair of the board of Sionna Therapeutics, Inc. He previously served on the boards of Exact Sciences, Xilio Therapeutics and Agios Pharmaceuticals, Inc. He is also an Executive Fellow at Harvard Business School and served as a Visiting Senior Lecturer of Finance at Cornell University's Graduate School of Management from 2021 through May 2026. Mr. Clancy holds a B.S. in Business Administration, with a Finance concentration, from Babson College and an M.B.A. from Columbia University.

Mr. Bell currently serves as Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of Alcon, where he oversees the company's commercial, manufacturing, quality, and regulatory operations. Prior to assuming this role in 2024, he served as President, Global Business & Innovation, leading product development across Alcon's surgical, vision care, and digital health businesses. Previously, he served as President, International and President of Alcon's Europe, Middle East and Africa region. Before joining Alcon in 2016, Mr. Bell held senior leadership positions at Hospira and Allergan and began his career with GlaxoSmithKline. He holds a Bachelor of Arts with honors in Economics from the University of York in the United Kingdom.

Mr. Clancy and Mr. Bell will be included in the company’s slate of director nominees in the proxy statement for Align’s 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Following the appointments of Messrs. Clancy and Bell, the Board will be composed of 13 directors until December 31, 2026, when the previously announced retirement of Mr. C. Raymond Larkin, Jr. will reduce the number of directors to 12.

About Align Technology, Inc.

Align Technology designs and manufactures the Invisalign® System, the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, iTero™ intraoral scanners and services, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software. These technology building blocks enable enhanced digital orthodontic and restorative workflows to improve patient outcomes and practice efficiencies for over 307 thousand doctor customers and are key to accessing Align’s 600 million consumer market opportunity worldwide. Over the past 29 years, Align has helped doctors treat approximately 24.2 million patients with the Invisalign System and is driving the evolution in digital dentistry through the Align™ Digital Platform, our integrated suite of unique, proprietary technologies and services delivered as a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients and consumers, orthodontists and GP dentists, and lab/partners. Williams brings significant industry and operational experience, including senior leadership of manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, and environmental, health and safety functions at The Dow Chemical Company.

"We are delighted to nominate Carol, a proven leader who would be a strong addition to the Board as it oversees Air Products' strategy and continued focus on safe, reliable execution to deliver long-term value for shareholders," said Wayne T. Smith, Chairman of the Board.

Williams spent 34 years at Dow in roles that included Executive Vice President of Manufacturing and Engineering, Supply Chain and Environmental, Health and Safety Operations; President of Chemicals and Energy; and Senior Vice President of Basic Chemicals. She retired at the end of 2014 as Special Advisor to the Chief Executive Officer. Williams serves on the boards of Olin Corporation, where she chairs the Nominating and Governance Committee, and O-I Glass, Inc. She holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from Carnegie Mellon University.

The Company also announced that Jessica Trocchi Graziano and Bhavesh ("Bob") Patel will not stand for re-election at the 2027 Annual Meeting and will retire from the Board when their terms conclude.

"We are grateful to Jessica and Bob for their service and contributions to Air Products," said Smith. "Both provided important insight and counsel during a period of significant change for the Company, and we thank them for their dedication and wish them well in their future endeavors."

VANCOUVER and GLIL YAM, Israel, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IM Cannabis Corp. ("IMC" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: IMCC), a medical cannabis company with operations in Israel, announces that the board of directors of the Company (the "Board") has approved a consolidation of its issued and outstanding common shares, no par value per share ("Common Shares") on the basis of one post-consolidated Common Share for every three pre-consolidated Common Shares (the "Consolidation").

The Board has authorized the Consolidation to be effected, with the Company currently expecting November 23, 2026 to be the effective date of the Consolidation (the "Effective Date"). The Company anticipates that the Common Shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market ("Nasdaq") on a post-Consolidation basis at the opening of trading on November 23, 2026, subject to final confirmation from Nasdaq and completion of applicable corporate, transfer agent and market implementation processes.

Upon the completion of the Consolidation, the CUSIP and ISIN of the Common Shares will be changed to 44969Q604 and CA44969Q6040, respectively. The Company's name and existing stock symbol "IMCC" will remain unchanged.

After giving effect to the Consolidation, the issued and outstanding Common Shares are expected to be reduced from 1,844,162 Common Shares to approximately 614,721 Common Shares, subject to rounding for fractional Common Shares. No fractional Common Shares will be issued in connection with the Consolidation. Instead, all fractional Common Shares equal to or greater than one-half resulting from the Consolidation will be rounded to the next whole number, otherwise, the fractional Common Share will be cancelled. The exercise price and/or conversion price and the number of Common Shares issuable under the Company's outstanding convertible, exchangeable or exercisable securities will be proportionately adjusted in connection with the Consolidation in accordance with their respective terms.

The primary purpose of the Consolidation is to increase the per-share trading price of the Common Shares in an effort to support the Company's efforts to maintain compliance with Nasdaq's US$1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing. Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), a company that fails to satisfy Nasdaq's US$1.00 minimum bid price requirement is ordinarily afforded a 180-calendar-day compliance period. However, under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv), a company is not eligible for that compliance period if it has effected a reverse share split during the prior one-year period. On August 27, 2026, the Company effected a 30:1 share consolidation. Accordingly, if the closing bid price of the Common Shares is below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, the Company would not be eligible for a compliance period and Nasdaq Staff would issue a Staff Delisting Determination with respect to the Common Shares. There can be no assurance that the Consolidation will result in the Company maintaining compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing requirements or that the Company will otherwise maintain the listing of its Common Shares on Nasdaq.

Registered shareholders as of the Effective Date will receive a letter of transmittal from Computershare Investor Services Inc., the Company's registrar and transfer agent for its Common Shares, providing instructions for the exchange of their Common Shares as soon as practicable following the Effective Date. Registered shareholders may also obtain a copy of the letter of transmittal by accessing the Company's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca. Until surrendered, each share certificate or direct registration system statement representing pre-consolidated Common Shares will represent the number of whole post-consolidated Common Shares to which the holder is entitled as a result of the Consolidation. No action is required by beneficial holders to receive post-consolidation Common Shares in connection with the Consolidation. Beneficial shareholders who hold their Common Shares through intermediaries (e.g., a broker, bank, trust company, investment dealer or other financial institution) and who have questions regarding how the Consolidation will be processed should contact their intermediaries with respect to the Consolidation.

IMC (Nasdaq: IMCC) is an international company currently operating a medical cannabis platform serving patients in Israel.

The IMC ecosystem operates in Israel through its subsidiaries, which import and distribute cannabis to medical patients, leveraging years of proprietary data and patient insights. The Company also operates medical cannabis retail pharmacies and online platforms in Israel that enable the safe delivery and quality control of IMC products throughout the value chain.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Panoro Minerals Ltd. (TSXV: PML) (BVL: PML) (OTCQB: POROF) (FSE: PZM) ("Panoro" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that a new metallurgical testwork program for the Company's Cotabambas Copper-Gold-Silver Project (the "Project") has commenced at the Certimin laboratory in Lima, Peru, under the supervision of Transmin Metallurgical Consultants (the "Program"). The current Program is using the process flowsheet evaluated in the superseded 2015 preliminary economic analysis (the "Superseded 2015 PEA"), as a reference point for metallurgical testing. Preliminary rougher flotation results indicate that the new samples are responding generally as expected in preliminary rougher flotation testing using that flowsheet as a reference point. The 2015 PEA does not reflect the current mineral resource estimate for the Project and is not a current economic evaluation of the Project. Optimization testwork is now underway to evaluate copper recovery, gold recovery, concentrate quality, with a view to informing capital cost and operating cost assumptions for future studies.

The response of the new samples in rougher flotation provides a solid basis for continuing to evaluate and optimize the process flowsheet used as a reference point for the current testwork. Our focus is on optimizing the process design to maximize recoveries and maintain a strong final concentrate grade for the Project. We look forward to reporting further results as they are received," says Luquman Shaheen, President and CEO.

The Company expects the next steps in the Program to include the following:

  • value optimization testwork seeking improved metal recoveries and the evaluation of performance at coarser grind sizes;

  • testwork aimed at optimization of cleaner flotation performance, maximizing value from both copper and gold recovery to the final concentrate; and

  • geometallurgical variability testing for key financial and engineering drivers, such as ore hardness, flotation response and concentrate quality to improve confidence in the metallurgical performance predictions to be used in coming studies.

About Panoro

Panoro is a Canadian mineral exploration and development company focused on advancing its 100% owned Cotabambas Copper, Gold and Silver Project, located in the Apurimac region in southern Peru. The Company is advancing its High-Grade Strategy to design an open-pit mine focused on the high-grade component of the mineral resource. The Cotabambas Project hosts:

Permit No. 10822, a Permit to Operate a Pipeline in Texas, authorizing operation of the Company's central Texas natural-gas pipeline system.

The permit follows a regulatory process that extended for more than one year and represents a major operating milestone for Olenox. With the permit now issued, the Company can move forward with the staged activation, restoration and expansion of the pipeline system while pursuing new natural-gas supply and power-generation opportunities.

The permit covers 95.19 miles of pipeline across Brown, Coleman and McCulloch counties and classifies the system as a gas utility. Olenox Corp. is identified as the pipeline owner, operator and economic operator. The permit was issued October 30, 2026 and is valid through May 31, 2028.

Olenox is currently working to secure an initial natural-gas capacity of approximately 1 million cubic feet per day ("MMcf/d") for the system. The Company plans to use that initial capacity to support the staged deployment of a 4-megawatt ("MW") containerized power-generation site, with initial power production targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

"Receiving this permit is a significant step forward for Olenox and the result of more than a year of regulatory and operational work," said Mike McLaren, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Olenox. "We can now begin moving this pipeline from an existing infrastructure asset into an operating platform for natural-gas transportation and distributed power generation. Our initial objective is to line up approximately 1 MMcf per day of gas capacity, deploy the first 4 MW site and build from there as pipeline throughput and market opportunities increase."

The initial 4 MW site is expected to serve as the first deployment under Olenox's broader strategy to develop multiple containerized power projects of 10 MW or less across the United States and Canada. The distributed model is designed to place scalable generating capacity near available energy resources and expand individual sites in stages as gas supply, infrastructure and customer demand support additional capacity.

Olenox intends to evaluate additional gas-supply arrangements, pipeline restoration requirements, compression and facility upgrades, and future off-take and power-generation opportunities across the system. As throughput increases, the Company expects to assess additional containerized generation deployments that could extend the economic value of the pipeline and its surrounding energy infrastructure.

The planned 1 MMcf/d capacity, 4 MW deployment, Q1 2027 production timeline and future project expansion are targets and have not yet been achieved. Development remains subject to securing gas supply, generation equipment, financing, site readiness, engineering, construction, interconnection, applicable permits and approvals, and other customary operating requirements.

Through its subsidiaries, Olenox is building a vertically integrated platform designed to connect energy resources with power-intensive infrastructure while delivering engineered and modular solutions across industrial markets.

The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report highlights growing consumer expectations around trust, business continuity and employee safety

WORCESTER, Mass., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- According to new research by The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc. (NYSE: THG) and Statista, 60% of respondents would temporarily shop with a competitor if their preferred small business closed due to an unexpected event, with more than half seeking alternatives within a week.

The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report: Reputation, Risk and Resilience examines the factors that most influence small business shoppers' trust and the events most likely to damage a business's reputation. Its findings underscore the role preparedness, employee safety and risk management play in helping small businesses maintain trust. The research found reliable products and services, protection of customer data, transparent communication and fair treatment of employees are among the factors respondents identify as most important in earning trust.

"Our research shows 87% of respondents say small businesses are important to their communities and 61% shop at a small business at least once a week," said Charles (Chip) F. Hamann, president of small commercial at The Hanover. "At the same time, the survey also underscores the importance of customer data protection, employee safety and business preparedness in earning and maintaining trust among consumers. Small businesses that proactively manage risk can strengthen customer confidence and position themselves to recover more effectively when disruptions occur. An independent agent is well positioned to help business owners navigate evolving risks, strengthen preparedness strategies and identify insurance solutions that support long-term resilience."

Trust extends beyond products and services

While reliable products and services remain the foundation of customer trust, the survey also explored other factors that may shape confidence in a business. When asked to rank the events that would be most likely to damage their trust in a small business, respondents most often placed the following among their top three:

  • Serious product safety issues (73%)
  • Customer data or privacy breaches (73%)
  • Employee safety or workplace treatment (69%)

Respondents also ranked the factors that were most important in earning their trust. Sixty-eight percent ranked reliable products and services in their top three factors. Protecting customer data followed with 62%. Lastly, transparent communication when problems occurred and treating employees fairly were among the top three factors for 54% of respondents.

Employee safety strengthens reliability

Respondents also associated employee safety with a greater likelihood of business success. Ninety-two percent of respondents agree small businesses that invest in employee safety are more likely to provide reliable service and remain successful over time. The finding suggests small business shoppers view employee safety as an indicator of operational stability and responsible business management.

To learn more about the findings from The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report: Reputation, Risk and Resilience, visit hanover.com. For more information on The Hanover's small business insurance solutions, please visit hanover.com/businesses.

The online survey was conducted by Statista+ on behalf of The Hanover from Sept. 2-4, 2026, among 500 U.S. consumers ages 18 to 64 who purchase products or services from small businesses at least once a month. For ranking questions, "top three" represents the percentage of respondents who placed a factor first, second or third.

Celebrates 160 years of customer service, implements vision for the future


SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- San Jose Water (“SJW” or “the Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of H2O America (NASDAQ: HTO), today unveiled H2O Next, one part of the company’s long-term vision to develop alternative water supply sources that provide affordable and sustainable local water supply to customers for generations to come, and shared the first look at the mobile water purification lab pilot facility and interactive experience. SJW, celebrating 160 years of service this month, expects the H2O Next lab to begin accepting visitors at its McLaughlin pumping station base location in fall 2027, ahead of the two-year timeline announced in April.

“When San Jose Water was founded in 1866, a promise to deliver good and pure water meant two tanks and about 400 neighbors,” said Tanya Moniz-Witten, president of San Jose Water. “Every generation since then has looked ahead to what this community would need next, and San Jose Water has been here to meet challenges in prudent, innovative ways for our customers. H2O Next is part of how we’ll continue doing that, and we look forward to this pilot demonstration and learning lab being accessible to customers and community members to see it up close, ask tough questions and help shape what comes next.”

About half of the water SJW delivers today is imported from outside of Silicon Valley, and H2O Next will demonstrate the technology SJW could use at scale to make purified recycled water an alternative local supply that holds up in drought conditions and meets customers’ expectations.

Lab visitors will be able to follow recycled water through each stage of the water purification process and see how the technology purifies it to meet strict federal and state drinking water standards. SJW experts will be available to answer questions. Community groups, schools and event organizers can request a visit to the lab. A new video featuring President Tanya Moniz-Witten and Jake Walsh, vice president of engineering, with a 3D tour of the planned mobile lab, is available at sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext.

Also on the innovation front, SJW is completing installation of its smart meters, finishing a three-year systemwide rollout by the end of 2026. The meters record water use every hour so customers can monitor their water usage and spot potential leaks early. SJW sent more than 44,000 leak notifications in 2025 and more than 100,000 through July 2026, giving customers practical, timely information they can use to reduce water loss and better manage household costs. Combined with acoustic leak detection on about 14,000 of the company’s 20,000 fire hydrants, the technology helps SJW find and fix problems before they become costly main breaks. Together, these technologies have helped SJW keep its water loss rate to about 8%, compared with a national average of roughly 14%.

Those tools build on steady investment in the water system behind every tap. Since 2021, SJW has invested more than $1 billion to upgrade infrastructure and replace pipes, tanks and well pumps. At its Cambrian Station, which serves about 225,000 people from Japantown to the Rose Garden, SJW brought the first of two new 8-million-gallon, seismically resilient tanks online in February, replacing earthen reservoirs that had served the community for more than a century. The company also performs more than 18,000 water quality tests each year across dozens of locations to confirm its teams and facilities meet water quality standards, and its security teams block roughly 5 million attempted cyberattacks every day to protect the systems that have kept water flowing for 160 years and will continue to serve Silicon Valley for generations to come.

To watch the H2O Next video and 3D tour, visit sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext. SJW’s 160th anniversary video is available at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r3eF_ajkXDw. Photos, video and background materials for media are available for download at sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext.

Founded in 1866, San Jose Water is a regulated private utility and one of the largest and most technically sophisticated urban water systems in the United States. The company serves more than one million people in the greater San Jose metropolitan area. San Jose Water is owned by H2O America, a publicly traded company listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the symbol HTO. H2O America also owns Connecticut Water Company in Connecticut, Maine Water Company in Maine and Texas Water Company in Texas. To learn more about San Jose Water, visit www.sjwater.com.

LOUDON, Tenn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Malibu Boats, Inc. (NASDAQ: MBUU), the global leader in performance sport boats, today announced the Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview, a global series of familiarization events that gives waterskiers the opportunity to get behind the Response TXi with AtmosDrive and experience the boat before competing on it. Running from December 2026 through February 2027, the series stops in Florida, along Australia’s east coast, and at the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships site in Peru.

As the exclusive official towboat partner of the International Waterski & Wakeboard Federation (IWWF), Malibu will tow all IWWF World Waterski Championships with the Response TXi with AtmosDrive, including the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships in Peru (Jan. 10–16, 2027), the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships in Australia (Feb. 16–21, 2027), and the 2028 IWWF World Over 35 Waterski Championships (Aug. 27–Sept. 3, 2028). The Worlds Preview gives athletes from every nation the chance to ski behind the boat well before they reach the start dock.

Having pulled 13 world records in waterskiing, the Response TXi is built on Malibu’s T-Cut Diamond Hull, allowing it to track precisely and leave a minimal wake. AtmosDrive delivers more of the engine’s pull into every set: jumpers feel it at the ramp, while slalom and trick skiers feel it through every pass. Many of the world’s top skiers have yet to ski behind the Response TXi, and the Worlds Preview is designed to change that by bringing the boat within reach before competition.

In the United States, the series arrives Dec. 18–20 with a three-day event at Champions Lake in Auburndale, Florida. Athletes from every IWWF member federation can ski timed sets in slalom, trick, and jump, with Will Asher joining Malibu representatives and event staff on the dock throughout the event.

In Australia, Malibu Boats Australia brings the Worlds Preview to four venues across Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland from Dec. 10 through Jan. 22, with priority for Australian Open and U21 team members. Sessions run at Bridgewater, Victoria (Dec. 10–11); Albury, New South Wales (Dec. 18 and 21–22); Marshalls, Queensland (Jan. 14–15), and Stoney Park, New South Wales (Jan. 18–19), with Australian Masters familiarization at Bridgewater on Jan. 22. The same boat will also tow three L-rated tournaments: the Bridgewater Malibu Series, the Albury Jump-Off, and the Australian Masters. For the two weeks before the Worlds, Feb. 1–5 and 8–12, the boat and site at Albury are open to competitors from every nation.

In Peru, two Response TXi boats with AtmosDrive will be at Bujama Lacus, site of the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships (Jan. 10–16, 2027), for official familiarization Jan. 10–12, ahead of preliminary rounds beginning Jan. 13.

Official familiarization and competition will be towed by:

Brand: Malibu
Model: Response TXi
Engine: Monsoon M6Di 430 HP (6.2 Liter)
Transmission: ZF 1.22:1
Speed Control: Zero Off, latest version
Slalom & Trick Prop: OJ 3090 – 4 Blade – 14 × 14
Jump Prop: OJ 3084 – 3 Blade – 14 × 13

“The work that happens before competition matters,” said Rachael Green, General Manager of Malibu Boats. “The TXi is built to give athletes the consistent pull and performance they need to focus on their skiing when it counts. The Worlds Preview gives skiers the chance to experience that performance firsthand and understand what makes the Response TXi a strong competition platform.”

“Confidence in the boat is what lets you push the limits,” added Will Asher, Malibu Pro Team skier. “I worked with our engineers on AtmosDrive so the pull would be something skiers can count on, pass after pass. When you trust the boat, you stop thinking about it and start chasing what’s possible. I’ll be on the dock in Florida to help skiers find that feeling for themselves.”

“The world is coming to Australian water, and the skiers deserve to know this boat long before it counts,” said Noel Gordon, Manufacturing & Process Engineer at Malibu Boats Australia. “From Bridgewater to Stoney Park, our Open and U21 teams will have the chance to log real sets behind the Response TXi all summer. Then, for the final two weeks, we open Albury to skiers from every nation, so when they reach the start dock, the boat already feels like home.”

The Worlds Preview underscores Malibu’s commitment to athlete development and to advancing waterskiing at every level, worldwide. More Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview events are to come, and Malibu will announce them once they are planned.

Malibu Boats, Inc. (NASDAQ: MBUU) is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of a diverse range of recreational powerboats, including performance sport, sterndrive, and outboard boats. Malibu Boats, Inc. is the market leader in the performance sport boat category through its Malibu and Axis boat brands, the leader in the 20’–40’ segment of the sterndrive boat category through its Cobalt brand, and in a leading position in the saltwater fishing boat market with its Pursuit and Cobia offshore boats and Pathfinder, Maverick, and Hewes flats and bay boat brands. A leading innovator in the powerboat industry, Malibu Boats, Inc. designs products for a growing range of recreational boaters, fishermen, and watersports enthusiasts who make boating a central part of their active lifestyles.
